title: Upselling & Suggestive Selling
blurb: How to make genuine, well-timed suggestions that improve the guest's visit and accept a no gracefully.
siteNotes: Current specials, signature dishes and wine pairings the team should know
legalNotes: No legal rules in this trainer; it is service good practice.

cards.kicker: Front of house and bar · 10 minutes
cards.title: Upselling & Suggestive Selling
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- make suggestions that feel like service
- time and word a suggestion well
- accept a no gracefully

cards.title: Upselling done well is service
cards.body:
Upselling has a bad reputation, but done well it is not pushy. It is helping guests enjoy their visit more while gently growing the bill.

> "Our sticky toffee pudding is famous, shall I bring one to share?"

items.title: Helpful
items.text: A suggestion that lands as service.

cards.title: Know your menu inside out
cards.body: You cannot recommend what you do not know. Learn the dishes, the specials, the wines and the cocktails, and which go well together. When you speak with genuine enthusiasm, guests trust the recommendation.

cards.title: Right moment, right words
cards.body: Suggest a starter or a side while they are choosing mains, a better wine to match the food, a dessert or coffee at the right moment. Descriptive language beats a flat question every time.

left.title: Say
items: "Warm, gooey and served with clotted cream"
A wine that matches the food
A side while they choose mains

right.title: Not
items: A suggestion after they have paid

cards.title: Respect a no
cards.body: Read the guest: suggest, do not pressure. If they say no, a cheerful "no problem at all" keeps the mood right and leaves the door open next time.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Upselling should improve the guest's experience first
- Know your menu and drinks inside out
- Use appetising, descriptive language at the right moment
- Suggest, never pressure
- Accept a no gracefully

cards.q: Done well, upselling can feel like great service rather than a sales pitch.
cards.why: A genuine suggestion at the right moment often lands as great service.

cards.q: What is the foundation that lets you upsell well?
options: A confident and lively manner at every table
A script from the manager to follow word for word
A clear sales target for every single shift
Knowing your menu and drinks inside out
cards.why: You cannot recommend what you do not know, so learn the dishes, specials, wines and cocktails.

cards.q: A good moment to suggest a side or starter is…
cards.why: Suggest a starter or side while they are choosing mains.

cards.q: Descriptive, appetising language works better than "do you want dessert?".
cards.why: "Warm, gooey and served with clotted cream" beats a flat question every time.

cards.q: If a guest says no to a suggestion, you should…
options: Offer a cheaper alternative straight away
Make a note to ask again at the table
cards.why: A cheerful "no problem at all" keeps the mood right and leaves the door open next time.

cards.q: You should recommend things with genuine enthusiasm.
cards.why: Genuine enthusiasm makes guests trust the recommendation.

cards.q: Upselling should always improve what for the guest first?
cards.why: The experience comes first; the extra spend follows naturally.

cards.q: You should pressure guests into buying more.
Suggesting a wine that matches the food is an example of…
options: Ignoring what the guest asked for
cards.why: Relevance and timing are what make a suggestion helpful.

cards.q: You cannot recommend a dish or drink well if you do not know it.
cards.why: Knowing your menu and drinks is the foundation of good upselling.
